items.title: How do you deal with AI Output of your boss?
items.raw_excerpt: So, my boss goes on a rampage. You can clearly see the joy and at the same time the rage and impatience. AI is the tool he always wanted. We are too slow. Process is out of the window. No need for sprints anymore. No planning, just doing. All people downstream must somehow adapt. Whenever i see now his automated messages in slack, my natural reaction is: why do i even bother reading that? Thats for machines to read. He does not need me? Clearly i am not made for that. items.title: AI coding interfaces make approval easy and understanding hard
items.raw_excerpt: Coding interfaces in 2026 are noisy. I prompt agents and watch a wall of tool calls and AI-generated text pile up until my eyes glaze over. Somewhere in that wall are decisions that need my approval, but the interface does little to help me understand them. It’s easy to slip into hitting “approve” just to keep the work moving.

items.title: Connecting Captions Local Private AI Interpreter
items.raw_excerpt:
Hi HN, I built Connecting Captions, a live captioning and translation overlay for macOS that runs entirely on-device. Nothing goes over the network: no API calls, no audio leaving your machine, and it keeps working offline. I wanted live translation I could use in meetings and conversations without worrying about connectivity, latency spikes, or sending sensitive audio to a third party. The technically interesting part is a low-latency, self-correcting pipeline for speech-to-text and translation. It has two modes: Sentence mode: buffers until a sentence boundary, then translates with full context. It’s more accurate, especially between languages with different word order.
Streaming mode: translates word by word as speech arrives, trading grammatical accuracy for minimal delay. Current stat
